MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MAY 6, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS AND TELECONFERENCED
  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held in a hybrid format that allowed members of the public to
participate in—person and remotely Via Zoom.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Mazza called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair John G. Mazza, Vice Chair Drew Leonard, Commissioners Kraig Hill
  and Dennis R. Smith

  ABSENT: Commissioner Skylar Peak

  ALSO PRESENT: Patrick Donegan, Assistant City Attorney; Richard Mollica. Planning
  Director; Tyler Eaton, Senior Planner; Fletcher Allen, Associate Planner; Brenna Wengert,
  Contract Planner; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Gail Duncan, Administrative Assistant
  and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Hill led the Pledge ofAllegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Hill seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda as recommended by staff.

SUBSTITUTE MOTION
  Vice Chair Leonard and Commissioner Smith seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda as recommended by staff with Item No. 5.A. continued to the May 20, 2024
  Regular Planning Commission meeting.

  The substitute motion was called and the motion failed 2—2, Commissioner Peak

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS
  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Hill noted the Malibu Times posted a portion of correspondence he
  sent to the City Council regarding the potential to ban large trucks on Pacific Coast
  Highway (PCH) to improve public safety in the form of a letter to the editor. He
  learned the existing prohibition was on trucks with more than three axles and only
  extended along PCH as far as Decker Canyon. Several other residents have
  observed an increase in this type oftraffic as well and he asked for staff to provide
  an update.

  Senate Bill 9 (8B9). referred to as the duplex housing bill. was recently challenged
  in a lawsuit by a group ofCharter cities. A Los Angeles Superior Courtjudge ruled
  that SB9 was unconstitutionak and that the legislature could not rely on an eventual
  increase in below market rate housing based on allowance for additional units in
  previously single-family zoning areas. Some of the cities involved in the appeal
  were coastal cities. Commissioner Hill requested an update from staff regarding the
  City’s position on SB9.

  In response to Commissioner Hill’s request for an update on enforcement against
  large trucks traveling along the restricted section 0f PCH. Planning Director
  Mollica stated that the City’s Public Safety Department investigation was underway
  and findings would be reported to the City Council.

  ln response to Commissioner Hill’s question regarding SB9, Assistant City
  Attorney Donegan noted that SB9 had passed the State legislature. However, the
  referenced lawsuit was only applicable to charter cities and given the likelihood for
  a future Superior Court decision on that case. the decision held limited practical
  application to the City ofMalibu.

  Chair Mazza asked Assistant City Attorney Donegan whether Malibu could
  become a Charter city.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes 0f May 6i 2024
  Page 3 of 10

In response to Chair Mazza, Assistant City Attorney Donegan responded that
Malibu could potentially become a Charter city in the future but noted that it was a
very lengthy process.

Commissioner Smith expressed agreement with Commissioner Hill’s concerns
regarding the dangers of heavy vehicles moving through Malibu on PCH.

Chair Mazza asked about the schedule for the Temporary Use Permit (TUP)
Ordinance City Council hearing.

In response to Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica stated the TUP Ordinance
hearing was currently scheduled for the June 10, 2024 City Council Regular
meeting.

Chair Mazza asked staff whether the Trancas Country Market had applied for TUPs
for summer events.

ln response to Chair Mazza‘ Recording Secretary Evans responded that n0 TUP
applications had been received for summer 2024 events at Traneas Country Market
to date.

Chair Mazza asked staff for an update on restaurant use of parking lots as space for
outdoor seating as part of Coronavirus Disease 201 9 (COVID) measures.

In response to Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica stated that two restaurants
had applied for Conditional Use Permit Amendments for outdoor dining areas
approved as part of COVID measures. Letters were sent to all restaurants which
had applied for outdoor seating to either remove the temporary seating areas or
apply for permits. He stated that in total there were two restaurants going through
the process and one violation was issued.

Commissioner Smith asked staffwhat would happen when La Paz opened and their
parking spaces began to be used for beach parking.

1n response to Commissioner Smith, Planning Director Mollica stated that he did
not believe there was a requirement for the development to provide public parking.
He noted he was not aware of the owner’s plans for monitoring parking. although
some shopping center owners employed security guards to ensure that their parking
lots were not used by beachgoers.

Chair Mazza remarked on the increased demand for parking during summer months
and the need for a solution.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutcs 0f May 6, 2024
  Page 4 of 10

Planning Director Mollica presented an update on Planning Department changes
and additions. Highlights included the joint launch of the development portal on
April 22‘“ with the Building Safety Department. He explained the purpose 0f the
portal and how it would streamline the permitting process and allow applicants to
monitor the status of their projects. He stated that in an effort to improve public
service on Tuesday and Thursdaya the busiest days of the week, more senior level
staff would be available to respond to questions at the counter from 8 a.m. to noon.
Code Enforcement Officers would work two weekends per month and the Code
Enforcement Manager would continue to monitor the hotline and email on
weekends. lf needed, Code Enforcement staff would be brought in or a concern
could be deferred to the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department. Planning
Director Mollica announced Gail Duncan’s promotion to the position of
Administrative Assistant and noted Administrative Assistant Carole Myers would
begin employment near the end of the month. He congratulated Patricia Salazar on
her 22”d anniversary with the City of Malibu and thanked her for her years of
serv1ce.

Vice Chair Leonard asked Planning Director Mollica to clarify the type of award
recently won by Environmental Sustainability Department Director Bundy’s team.

In response to Vice Chair Leonard. Planning Director Mollica stated he did not
know the official name of the award. but noted it amounted to being named the
Building Safety department of the year within the State of California. He offered
his congratulations to the Building Safety Division.

Commissioner Hill asked staff for the reason the City code had moved to a new
website.

In response to Commissioner Hill. Planning Director Mollica noted that the City
code moved to eeode360.com as part of an initiative from the City Clerk’s office.
He explained that the new website made it easier to search for specific sections of
code and helped readers understand context with inclusion of a historical overview
ofcode amendments. He remarked that from a planning perspective. the new code
website would be an asset for case planners’ research.

In response to Planning Director Mollica, Commissioner Hill stated that he was
glad to hear the website would help staff. He asked staff to clarify what the Code
Enforcement hotline number was.

Planning Director Mollica clarified that the Code Enforcement hotline was a
voicemail, which could be reached (3 10) 456-2489. extension 484. He stated that
Code Enforcement Manager Cleavenger checked the hotline throughout the
weekend.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of May 6, 2024
  Pagc 5 of 10

Chair Mazza asked staff ifthe City could add thc Code Enforcement phone number
to both the website and City Manager updates and inform the public to call City
Code Enforcement with active concerns on weekends. He suggested the hotline
extension be added to the automated message for the City Hall phone outside of
normal operating hours.

In response to Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica stated the City could add
the hotline number to the website and City Manager updates. He agreed to
investigate whether the City Hall automated message could be modified to include
the hotline extension.

Chair Mazza asked staff if Code Enforcement would be scheduled during evening
hours to investigate potential Dark Sky Ordinance violations.

In response to Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica noted that Dark Sky
Ordinance complaints could be followed up on during daylight hours as well
because staff analysis was typically based on the code compliance of the light
fixtures.

Chair Mazza asked whether members of the public would be able to use the online
portal to access proposed developments and obtain information on applications.

ln response to Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica noted that the primary focus
ofthe portal was to streamline submittal of applications, although portal functions
were still undergoing further development. He noted that the eventual goal would
be to allow certain application submittal materials to be public. however some
documents would remain private in order to protect personally identifiable
information.

Chair Mazza asked staff if the public should use OnBase or the development portal
to look up information on a particular property.

Planning Director Mollica clarified that OnBase was still the primary record holder
for the City of Malibu and that any links in the Development Portal would work
through OnBase.

Commissioner Smith asked staff how quickly appeals to City Council were being
turned around. He noted that it appeared the process had been taking longer than in
prior years.

In response to Commissioner Smith. Planning Director Mollica explained that
appeals placed a demand on limited staff resources and had an extensive review
period with the City Attorney”s office before they could be finalized. The City
Council typically did not have adequate time for more than one appeal per meeting.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of‘May 6, 2024
  Page 6 of 10

  Vice Chair Leonard asked staff for the total number of appeals pending a City
  Council hearing and how long they had been waiting to be heard.

  In response to Vice Chair Leonard, Recording Secretary Evans noted there were
  currently scven appeals pending, either scheduled with a tentative City Council
  hearing date or waitlisted for a tentative date. She stated the next appeal scheduled
  to be heard by City Council was appealed on July 27, 2023. Hearing dates for
  appeals to City Council were subject to continuance when the Council required the
  meeting to hear other items with citywide impact.
